references.text: The sin offering is mentioned again in connection with atonement at the altar
The same instruction to burn the bull's flesh, skin, and entrails outside the camp for a sin offering
The bull shall be burned outside the camp, just as with the first sin offering
Moses carries out this command and burns the bull outside the camp
The flesh and the skin were burned with fire outside the camp
On the Day of Atonement, the sin offering's bull and goat shall be burned outside the camp
The red heifer shall be burned outside the camp along with its skin, flesh, and dung
The Letter to the Hebrews connects this with Jesus' suffering outside the city gate as a fulfillment of the sin offering's foreshadowing
Describes the same ritual procedure for a sin offering where the blood is brought in for atonement while the body is burned outside the camp.
A prophetic image confirming the same theological principle of removing the sin offering's body from the sanctuary.
Expands on the instruction from Exodus by specifying that the burning must take place in a clean place outside the camp.
Uses the ritual from Exodus as a theological image to explain Jesus' suffering outside the city walls.
